correctness.rationale: Each input one is counted twice among same-layer neighbor sums and once in the opposite layer. A predecessor of outer-all-one/inner-all-zero therefore has 2A+B>=2n and A+2B<=n. Together they force B=0, A=n. The target is itself fixed by the two same-layer neighbors and complementation commutes with the rule, giving two singleton basins in the entire stated family. For the Dürer census I independently evaluated all 4096 states using pairwise bitwise majority and a fresh first-repeat trace for every start. The sorted cycle suffix uniquely identifies each temporal attractor, grouping both phases of each two-cycle. This reproduced all 15 basin sizes with their multiplicities, the complete entry histogram by period, two consensus basins of 736, and precisely the singleton states 63 and 4032. The witness trajectory 79,263,70,257,64,0 first becomes periodic at update five; at time four it is not periodic, so F^6=F^4 fails while F^7=F^5 holds. Only inner vertices lie on triangles, so the two layers are invariant under automorphisms; every symmetry of the outer cycle extends, and the spokes force its unique extension. The independent quotient computation gave 7 fixed and 31 two-cycle classes and Burnside sums 84 and 372.
residual_risks: The full tables are exact for this labelled graph and synchronous open-neighbor rule, not for arbitrary GP(n,k). Only the isolation lemma generalizes here.

evidence: General finite majority theory gives period at most two and a bound by the number of edges as stated in the local certification paper. On this graph that bound is 18.
Benjamini et al. give an almost-sure period bound under their graph/invariance assumptions.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither general bound fixes the sharp transient of five or gives individual functional-graph components, predecessor fibers, or the orbit quotient. The new computation does not reclaim eventual period at most two.

evidence: Recurrent count papers restrict to configurations already satisfying F(x)=x or F^2(x)=x.
The perfect-coloring literature is a plausible match for identifying fixed layer colorings; the indexed description concerns admissible parameter matrices, and the primary full text was inaccessible.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A two-color partition with one opposite and two same-color neighbors identifies a fixed point but does not itself rule out nonfixed preimages. The summed predecessor inequalities give precisely that missing property on every stated graph. Similarly, aggregate recurrent counts and a coarse upper bound do not mechanically determine the basin spectrum or the sharp entry histogram.

evidence: A prior all-size recurrent census directly lists 14 fixed points and 184 two-cycle orbits for GP(6,2); a separate fixed-point theorem also gives 14. The former explicitly excludes basins and entry times, the latter covers fixed points only.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Credit prior exact coverage of the recurrent counts. Those counts sum roots/cycles, not the numbers of configurations flowing to each, or the automorphism action on those orbits. No separate exact Dürer basin/entry table was found in the material examined.

originality.rationale: The closest indexed prior theorem includes the exact recurrent population on the identical graph and expressly excludes the basin and transient questions. Those recurrent totals are context, not a contribution under review. Other records classify basins on different generalized Petersen graphs or with different state alphabets. The isolation proof gives uniqueness of the predecessor, not just a new way to identify an already-known polarized fixed point.
residual_risks: A separate unindexed census or a stronger theorem about preimages of perfect colorings may exist; the perfect-coloring primary article and original Goles–Olivos paper were not read in full. Unrelated or deferred search queries were not used as negative evidence.

value.rationale: This supplies precise basin and transient reference data for a named cubic graph in an already studied majority-dynamics family. The exact populations distinguish recurrent abundance from its dynamical reach, and the sharp fixed-only final entry layer is information not present in a period bound. The matching-spoke isolation argument also identifies recurrent states that cannot be reached from any other start, for a natural whole family rather than just the instance audited.
residual_risks: The finite census does not explain general basin-size asymptotics across the family; the structural conclusion concerns the two polarized states.
